column3: Questions any human claim to see the unseen, supporting the access boundary.
Names the knower of unseen and witnessed reality, grounding the source distinction.
Offers a secondary case where unseen history reaches the messenger through revelation.
Shows unseen content can be conveyed through a trustworthy messenger without ordinary access.
Immediate exception: a chosen messenger receives a guarded, permitted disclosure.
Generic divine knowledge adds no distinct point about unseen access.
Parallels the unseen-and-witnessed formula, though it repeats the core attribution.
Earlier jinn uncertainty about a future outcome frames the surah's later knowledge boundary.
Its making-manifest language supplies a secondary sense of disclosure, not unseen knowledge itself.
The nearby prohibition on calling anyone alongside God weakly echoes exclusive authority.
Generic knowledge in an entrance-and-recompense setting is not an access claim.

Repeats the unseen-and-witnessed attribution with no new access mechanism.

A secondary access-control analogy: what becomes manifest depends on authorized conditions.

Joins truth-bearing proclamation to the one who fully knows hidden matters.

Explicitly includes secret and private counsel within God's knowledge of hidden things.

Concealment eventually uncovered offers a secondary hidden-to-manifest pattern.

The divine command becoming manifest is a secondary public-disclosure parallel.

Repeats the challenge to claims of possessing and writing from the unseen; redundant with 52:41.
Whispered adornment and its reception do not define the unseen-access boundary.

Attributes the unseen of heavens and earth to God and excludes partners in judgment.

Defers an unknown duration to the Lord, then redirects to actionable caution.

Places what is absent from sight in a clear record, a secondary account of hidden content.
Repeats divine knowledge of unseen and witnessed reality without adding a new exception.
Its ignorance concerns impending punishment, only indirectly related to concealed knowledge.
Uses hidden-and-visible knowledge as the basis for judgment amid disagreement.
Public predominance is an appearance reading, not a disclosure of the unseen.

Unique punishment does not inform the focus verse's access rule.
A broad hidden-and-visible formula in creation and judgment adds little beyond earlier parallels.

Explicitly denies that even the smallest matter escapes the knower of the unseen.
